claim: Germline inactivation of Rps27l triggers ribosomal stress to stabilize Mdm2.
source: Germline inactivation of Rps27l triggers ribosomal stress to stabilize Mdm2, which degrades Mdm4 to reduce Mdm2-Mdm4 E3 ligase towards p53
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing B23 nucleoplasm staining and enhanced ribosomal protein-Mdm2 binding upon Rps27l disruption, along with measurements of Mdm2 protein stability.

claim: Stabilized Mdm2 degrades Mdm4 to reduce Mdm2-Mdm4 E3 ligase activity towards p53.
source: Germline inactivation of Rps27l triggers ribosomal stress to stabilize Mdm2, which degrades Mdm4 to reduce Mdm2-Mdm4 E3 ligase towards p53
evidence: Supported by data showing increased Mdm4 ubiquitylation, shortened Mdm4 protein half-life, and reduced Mdm2-Mdm4 complex formation in Rps27l-null MEFs.

claim: Rps27l disruption leads to p53-dependent apoptotic depletion of hematopoietic stem cells.
source: leading to p53-dependent apoptotic depletion of hematopoietic stem cells and postnatal death, which is rescued by Trp53 deletion
evidence: Demonstrated by flow cytometry showing reduced HSPCs, increased Annexin V staining, cleaved caspase-3 accumulation, and rescue by Trp53 deletion.

claim: Rps27l disruption causes postnatal death that is rescued by Trp53 deletion.
source: leading to p53-dependent apoptotic depletion of hematopoietic stem cells and postnatal death, which is rescued by Trp53 deletion
evidence: Kaplan-Meier survival curves show that Rps27l-/-;Trp53-/- mice survive while Rps27l-/- mice die postnatally.

claim: Under Trp53+/- background, Rps27l disruption triggers genomic instability.
source: whereas under Trp53+/− background, Rps27l disruption triggers genomic instability and Trp53 deletion to promote tumorigenesis
evidence: Metaphase analysis shows ~63% aneuploidy rate in lymphomas from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice and increased aneuploidy in primary MEFs.

claim: Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice develop lymphomas at higher incidence than Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/- mice.
source: Paradoxically, while increased p53 is expected to inhibit tumorigenesis, Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/− mice develop lymphomas at higher incidence with p53 loss-of-heterozygosity
evidence: Kaplan-Meier survival curves show significantly shorter survival in Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice compared to Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/- mice (p=0.0036).

claim: Lymphomas in Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice exhibit p53 loss-of-heterozygosity.
source: Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/− mice develop lymphomas at higher incidence with p53 loss-of-heterozygosity and severe genome aneuploidy
evidence: PCR amplification of Trp53 exons shows deletion of wild-type Trp53 allele in 97% of tumor tissues genotyped.

claim: Lymphomas in Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice exhibit severe genome aneuploidy.
source: Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/− mice develop lymphomas at higher incidence with p53 loss-of-heterozygosity and severe genome aneuploidy
evidence: Metaphase analysis shows ~63% aneuploidy rate in lymphomas, which is higher than the 30-35% rate in Trp53-null mice.

claim: Rps27l disruption imposes a selection pressure against p53.
source: suggesting that Rps27l disruption impose a selection pressure against p53
evidence: In 97% of tumors from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice, the wild-type Trp53 allele was deleted, indicating selection against p53.

claim: p53 is frequently inactivated during human carcinogenesis by point mutation in 50% of human cancers.
source: p53 is frequently inactivated during human carcinogenesis either by point mutation which occurs in 50% of human cancers (Greenblatt et al., 1994)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Greenblatt et al., 1994.

claim: Mdm2 is a direct p53 target.
source: Mdm2 is a direct p53 target.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by multiple citations in the manuscript.

claim: Mdm2 inactivates p53 by binding to its transactivation domain and blocking its transactivation activity.
source: Mdm2 inactivates p53 through at least two main mechanisms: (a) binding to p53 at its transactivation domain and blocking its transactivation activity
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Haupt et al., 1997; Honda et al., 1997; Kubbutat et al., 1997.

claim: Mdm2 serves as an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote rapid degradation of p53.
source: (b) serving as an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote a rapid degradation of p53 (Haupt et al., 1997; Honda et al., 1997; Kubbutat et al., 1997; Fang et al., 2000; Honda and Yasuda, 2000)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: p53-Mdm2 forms an auto-regulatory feedback loop to keep p53 levels under control.
source: Thus, p53-Mdm2 forms an auto-regulatory feedback loop to keep p53 levels under control (Wu et al., 1993)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Wu et al., 1993.

claim: Mdm4 binds to p53 transactivation domain to block its transcription activity.
source: it does bind to p53 transactivation domain to block its transcription activity (Shvarts et al., 1996)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Shvarts et al., 1996.

claim: Mdm4 forms a tight 1:1 complex with Mdm2 via their respective C-terminal RING finger domains.
source: Mdm4 forms a tight 1:1 complex with Mdm2 via their respective C-terminal RING finger domains (Sharp et al., 1999; Tanimura et al., 1999)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Sharp et al., 1999 and Tanimura et al., 1999.

claim: Mdm2-Mdm4 heterodimers are the preferred dimer form compared to Mdm2-Mdm2 or Mdm4-Mdm4 homodimers.
source: and the Mdm2-Mdm4 heterodimers are the preferred dimer form, compared to the Mdm2-Mdm2 or Mdm4-Mdm4 homodimers (Kostic et al., 2006)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Kostic et al., 2006.

claim: Mdm4 is a direct substrate of Mdm2 for targeted ubiquitylation and degradation.
source: Furthermore, Mdm4 is a direct substrate of Mdm2 for targeted ubiquitylation and degradation (de Graaf et al., 2003; Kawai et al., 2003; Pan and Chen, 2003)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to de Graaf et al., 2003; Kawai et al., 2003; Pan and Chen, 2003.

claim: The Mdm2-Mdm4 heterodimer has optimal E3 ligase activity and is required for p53 degradation.
source: both in vitro cell culture studies using Mdm2 mutants (Kawai et al., 2007; Poyurovsky et al., 2007; Uldrijan et al., 2007) and in vivo studies using knock-in mice of Mdm2 and Mdm4 mutants (Itahana et al., 2007; Huang et al., 2011; Pant et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011) demonstrated that the Mdm2-Mdm4 heterodimer has an optimal E3 ligase activity and is required for p53 degradation
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations to both in vitro and in vivo studies.

claim: RPS27L is an 84-amino acid ribosomal like protein that differs from RPS27 by only three amino acids at the N-terminus.
source: RPS27L (NM_015920) is an 84-amino acid ribosomal like protein, which differs from its family member RPS27 (NM_001030) by only three amino acids (R5K, L12P, K17R) at the N-terminus
evidence: This is a factual description of the protein structure supported by sequence information.

claim: RPS27L is a direct p53 inducible target.
source: We and the others found that RPS27L is a direct p53 inducible target (He and Sun, 2007; Li et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to He and Sun, 2007 and Li et al., 2007.

claim: RPS27L directly binds to MDM2 and is subjected to MDM2-mediated ubiquitylation and degradation.
source: Our recent cell-based study showed that RPS27L directly binds to MDM2 and is subjected to MDM2-mediated ubiquitylation and degradation (Xiong et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work (Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: RPS27L competes with p53 for MDM2 binding, consequently inhibiting MDM2-mediated p53 ubiquitylation and degradation.
source: Furthermore, RPS27L competes with p53 for MDM2 binding, consequently inhibiting MDM2-mediated p53 ubiquitylation and degradation (Xiong et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work (Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: Rps27l-/- mice are about 50% in size and body weight compared to wild type and heterozygous littermates.
source: Compared to the wild type and heterozygous littermates, Rps27l−/− mice were about 50% in size and body weight (Figure 1B,C)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1B,C showing photographs and weight measurements.

claim: The weight of thymus and spleen is significantly reduced in Rps27l-/- mice at P8-10 after normalization with body weight.
source: At the organ levels after normalization with the body weight, the weight in the thymus and spleen was significantly reduced in Rps27l−/− mice at P8–10 (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1D showing organ weight measurements.

claim: Bone marrow derived from Rps27l-/- mice have much reduced cellularity.
source: The H&E staining revealed that the bone marrow derived from Rps27l−/− mice have much reduced cellularity (Figure 1E)
evidence: This is supported by H&E staining images shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The Rps27l-/- thymus shows a remarkable reduction in the thymic cortex with thymocytes undergoing apoptosis.
source: Likewise, the Rps27l−/− thymus showed a remarkable reduction in the thymic cortex, and thymocytes in cortical and cortical-medullary junction areas undergo apoptosis with accumulation of small irregular nuclear fragments (Figure 1F, arrows)
evidence: This is supported by H&E staining images shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Induction of apoptosis in Rps27l-/- mice is confirmed by immunofluorescent staining with antibody against cleaved caspase-3 in both thymocytes and bone marrow cells.
source: Induction of apoptosis was further confirmed by the immunofluorenscent staining with antibody against cleaved caspase-3 in both thymocytes (Figure 1G) and bone marrow cells (Figure 1H)
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence images shown in Figures 1G and 1H.

claim: Apoptosis in Rps27l-/- thymus is detectable by immunoblotting showing increased levels of cleaved caspase-3 and pro-apoptotic protein Puma.
source: Moreover, apoptosis in thymus was readily detectable by immunoblotting, which showed increased levels of cleaved caspase-3 and pro-apoptotic protein Puma (Figure 1I)
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Increased apoptosis is observed in myeloid progenitors derived from E14.5 Rps27l-/- fetal livers as reflected by Annexin V staining.
source: An increased apoptosis, as reflected by Annexin V staining (Figure 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F), but not reduced proliferation, as reflected by BrdU incorporation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G) was also seen in myeloid progenitors (MP), derived from E14.5 Rps27l−/− fetal livers
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1J and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: No reduced proliferation is observed in myeloid progenitors derived from E14.5 Rps27l-/- fetal livers as reflected by BrdU incorporation.
source: An increased apoptosis, as reflected by Annexin V staining (Figure 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F), but not reduced proliferation, as reflected by BrdU incorporation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G) was also seen in myeloid progenitors (MP), derived from E14.5 Rps27l−/− fetal livers
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Postnatal death of Rps27l knockout mice is likely associated with enhanced apoptosis leading to bone marrow depletion.
source: Thus, Rps27l is required for postnatal development of some organs, particularly thymus, spleen and bone marrow, and postnatal death of Rps27l knockout mice is likely associated with enhanced apoptosis, leading to bone marrow depletion
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed apoptosis and bone marrow depletion data.

claim: Rps27l-/- fetal livers show reduced size and total cell numbers compared to wild type.
source: Reduced size and total cell numbers in Rps27l−/− fetal livers. Representative fetal livers of three genotypes were photographed (A), and the numbers of fetal liver cells from E14.5 embryos were counted
evidence: This is supported by photographs and cell count data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: Decreased percentages and absolute numbers of HSPCs are observed in Rps27l-/- fetal livers.
source: Decreased percentages and absolute numbers of HSPCs in Rps27l−/− fetal livers. Cells from E14.5 fetal livers of Rps27l−/− (n = 7), Rps27l+/+ (n = 10), and Rps27l+/− (n = 8) were stained with antibodies against various surface markers. The populations of LSK (C and D), MP, CMP, GMP, and MEP (E and F) were analyzed by flow cytometry
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figures 2C-F.

claim: Recipient mice transplanted with Rps27l-/- fetal liver cells have significantly shorter survival than those transplanted with Rps27l+/+ cells in non-competitive reconstitution assay.
source: Kaplan–Meier survival curves of recipient mice after transplantation. Rps27l−/− or Rps27l+/+ fetal liver cells were injected, respectively, into recipient mice (n = 5, for each genotype). p = 0.0026
evidence: This is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival curve data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Dramatic reduction of donor-type (CD45.2) blood cells is observed in recipients transplanted with Rps27l-/- fetal livers in competitive reconstitution assay.
source: Dramatic reduction of donor-type (CD45.2) blood cells in recipients transplanted with Rps27l−/− fetal livers. The percentages of CD45.2+ cells in peripheral blood at 4, 12, and 20 weeks post transplantation were summarized
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figures 2J and 2K.

claim: HSPCs from Rps27l-/- fetal livers are unable to reconstitute sterilized bone marrow.
source: By both noncompetitive and competitive reconstruction assays, we clearly demonstrated that the HSPCs from Rps27l−/− fetal livers were unable to reconstitute sterilized bone marrow
evidence: This is supported by transplantation assay data shown in Figures 2H, 2J, and 2K.

claim: p53 accumulates in Rps27l-/- fetal livers and bone marrows as shown by immunostaining.
source: Representative p53 staining in fetal livers and bone marrows. Fetal livers at E14.5 and bone marrows at P6 were immuno-stained with p53 Ab. Arrows point to p53 positive staining
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining images shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Accumulation of p53 and Puma is observed in Rps27l-/- fetal livers by immunoblotting.
source: Accumulation of p53 and Puma in Rps27l−/− fetal livers. Fetal livers isolated from embryos of non-irradiated or irradiated pregnant Rps27l−/− females (E14.5) were lysed for IB at 5 hr after ionizing radiation at 5 Gy
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Accumulation of p53 and p53 targets is observed in Rps27l-/- spleens.
source: Accumulation of p53 and p53 targets in Rps27l+/− spleens. Several spleens with the same genotype from P6 pups were harvested, pooled, homogenized, and subjected to IB
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Accumulation of p53 and p53 targets is observed in Rps27l-/- brains.
source: Accumulation of p53 and p53 targets in Rps27l−/− brains. Brains from P8–10 pups were harvested and lysed for IB
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Accumulation of p53 and p53 target proteins is observed in Rps27l-/- MEFs.
source: Accumulation of p53 and p53 target proteins in Rps27l−/− MEFs. Two independent pairs of MEFs from embryos at E13.5 were lysed for IB with indicated antibodies
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Higher p53 levels are induced by ribosomal stress and DNA damaging agent, but not by endoplasmic reticulum stress in Rps27l-/- MEFs.
source: Higher p53 levels induced by ribosomal stress and DNA damaging agent, not by endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in Rps27l−/− MEFs. MEFs were treated with 5 nM Actinomycin D (ActD) for 24 hr, 5 μg/ml tunicamycin (Tm) for 8 hr, or 50 μM etoposide (Etop) for 24 hr, followed by IB
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Higher p53 levels are induced by ionizing radiation in Rps27l-/- MEFs.
source: Higher p53 levels induced by ionizing radiation in Rps27l−/− MEFs. MEFs were harvested for IB at various time points post 6 Gy of ionizing radiation
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Rps27l disruption extends protein half-lives of p53 and Mdm2.
source: Extension of protein half-lives of p53 and Mdm2 upon Rps27l disruption. Rps27l+/+ or Rps27l−/− MEFs were harvested at various time points post CHX treatment for IB (top). Densitometry quantification was performed with ImageJ, and the decay curves are shown (bottom)
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Rps27l disruption extends p53 protein half-life from approximately 18 minutes to 40 minutes.
source: We then measured the Mdm2 protein half-life and Mdm2 self-ubiquitylation in Rps27l+/+ vs Rps27l−/− MEFs and found that Rps27l disruption extends Mdm2 protein half-life from ∼18 min to 40 min (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Rps27l disruption impairs the ubiquitylation of endogenous p53 in vivo.
source: Rps27l disruption impairs the ubiquitylation of endogenous p53 in vivo. Rps27l+/+ or Rps27l−/− MEFs were harvested after 4 hr of MG132 treatment for IP with p53 Ab or normal IgG control, followed by IB with p53 Ab
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Rps27l disruption impairs p53 ubiquitylation in vitro.
source: Rps27l disruption impairs p53 ubiquitylation in vitro. The Mdm2-Mdm4 E3 and p53 (substrate) complex was immunoprecipitated with Mdm2 Ab from MG132 treated Rps27l+/+ or Rps27l−/− MEFs, and added into an in vitro ubiquitylation reaction mixture containing ATP, ubiquitin, E1, and E2 (UbcH5b)
evidence: This is supported by in vitro ubiquitylation assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Reduced Mdm2 self-ubiquitylation is observed upon Rps27l depletion.
source: Reduced Mdm2 self-ubiquitylation upon Rps27l depletion. Rps27l+/+ or Rps27l−/− MEFs were treated with MG132 for 4 hr before being harvested for IB using indicated Abs
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: RPS27L negatively regulates MDM2 protein levels in p53-null H1299 cells.
source: Negative regulation of MDM2 protein levels by RPS27L. p53-null H1299 lung cancer cells were transfected with MDM2 alone, or in combination with two concentrations of FLAG-tagged RPS27L for 48 hr (top), or infected with lenti-virus targeting RPS27L or scrambled control siRNA for 3 days (bottom), followed by IB with indicated Abs
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data in p53-null cells shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Reduced Mdm4 protein level is observed in Rps27l-/- MEFs.
source: Reduced Mdm4 protein level in Rps27l−/− MEFs. Two independent pairs of MEFs were harvested and subjected to IB with indicated Abs
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Reduced Mdm2-Mdm4 complex is observed in Rps27l-/- MEFs.
source: Reduced Mdm2-Mdm4 complex in Rps27l−/− MEFs. Whole cell extracts of Rps27l+/+ or Rps27l−/− MEFs were subjected to IP with Mdm2 Ab or normal IgG control, followed by IB with Mdm4 Ab (left), or subjected to IP with Mdm4 Ab or normal IgG control, followed by IB with Mdm2 Ab (right)
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Acute depletion of Rps27l causes sequential changes with Mdm2 elevation starting at 24 hr, followed by Mdm4 depletion starting at 48 hr, and p53 accumulation starting at 72-84 hr.
source: Compared to the Ad-GFP controls, acute depletion of Rps27l caused an elevated Mdm2, starting at 24 hr post Ad-Cre infection and lasting up to 96 hr, followed by depletion of Mdm4, starting at 48 hr. A moderate accumulation of p53 was not seen until the later time points, starting at 72–84 hr following Ad-Cre infection (Figure 4H)
evidence: This is supported by time-course immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Mdm2 accumulation followed by Mdm4 reduction upon Rps27l depletion is independent of p53.
source: Furthermore, Mdm2 accumulation, followed by Mdm4 reduction, is independent of p53, since a similar changing pattern was seen when Rps27lfl/fl;Trp53−/− MEFs were infected with Ad-Cre (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: This is supported by time-course immunoblotting data in Trp53-null MEFs shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: No change in p53 transcription is observed upon Rps27l disruption, but an increase in transcription of p53 targets is observed.
source: No change in p53 transcription, but an increase in transcription of p53 targets. Four independent pairs of MEFs were harvested for quantitative real-time PCR using indicated primers
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No change in p53 protein synthesis is observed upon Rps27l disruption.
source: No change in p53 protein synthesis. Two independent pairs of MEFs were treated with 50 μM MG132 for 1 hr, and then labeled with [35S]-methionine, followed by IP with p53 Ab
evidence: This is supported by [35S]-methionine labeling data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Rps27l is a ribosomal protein that co-sediments with 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits and 80S monosomes.
source: Rps27l is a ribosomal protein. Rps27l+/+ or Rps27l−/− MEFs were treated with CHX for 30 min before harvesting for ribosomal profiling. The cytoplasmic extracts were loaded on sucrose gradients (10%–50%) and subjected to ultra-centrifugation. Gradients were then fractionated and measured by optical density at 254 nm (top). The fractions from Rps27l+/+ MEFs were subjected to IB using indicated Abs (bottom)
evidence: This is supported by ribosomal profiling data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: B23 is released from nucleoli upon Rps27l depletion.
source: B23 is released from nucleoli upon Rps27l depletion. MEFs with indicated genotypes were left untreated or treated with 5 nM Act D for 24 hr, followed by immunofluoresent staining of B23 (left). Scale bar represents 20 µm. Cells with nucleolus and/or nucleoplasmic B23 staining were counted and expressed as percentage of total cells (at least 200) counted (right)
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Approximately 25% of Rps27l-/- MEFs show nucleoplasm B23 staining compared to approximately 7% of Rps27l+/+ MEFs.
source: While only ∼7% of Rps27l+/+ MEFs had nucleoplasm staining, ∼25% of Rps27l−/− MEFs had positive nucleoplasm staining (p <0.01) (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is supported by quantification of immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Increased Mdm2 binding of Rpl11, Rpl23, Rps7, Rps14, and Rps27, but not Rpl5, Rps27a, and Rps19 is observed in Rps27l-/- MEFs.
source: we did detect in Rps27l−/− MEFs an increased Mdm2 binding of Rpl11, Rpl23, Rps7, Rps14, and Rps27, but not Rpl5, Rps27a, and Rps19 (Figure 5C)
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Activation of p53 by Rps27l-deficiency is dependent on Rpl11, but not Rpl5.
source: silencing of Rpl11 (with enhanced Mdm2 binding upon Rps27l disruption), but not Rpl5 (without changing Mdm2 binding) abrogated the p53 activation in Rps27l−/− MEFs, suggesting activation of p53 by Rps27l-deficiency is dependent on Rpl11, but not Rpl5 (Figure 5D,E)
evidence: This is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figures 5D and 5E.

claim: Rps27l loss does not impair the transcription of rDNA.
source: Rps27l loss does not impair the transcription of rDNA. Four independent pairs of MEFs were harvested for quantitative real-time PCR using primers for 45S rRNA
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: No change in 28S and 18S rRNA levels is observed upon Rps27l disruption.
source: No change in 28S and 18S rRNA levels upon Rps27l disruption. Four pairs of MEFs from two independent litters were harvested for RNA extraction. Equal amounts of RNA were analyzed by formaldehyde gel electrophoresis with ethidium bromide staining
evidence: This is supported by RNA gel electrophoresis data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Rps27l loss moderately affects the kinetics of rRNA processing.
source: Rps27l loss moderately affects the kinetics of rRNA processing. Two independent pairs of MEFs were pulse labeled with L-[methyl-3H]-methionine, and chased for the indicated times. Total RNA was isolated and subjected to Northern blotting
evidence: This is supported by pulse-chase rRNA processing data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Rps27l loss has no effect on general protein synthesis.
source: Rps27l loss had no effect on general protein synthesis, as determined by a [35S]-methionine pulse-chase experiment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F)
evidence: This is supported by [35S]-methionine incorporation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Increased Mdm4 ubiquitylation is observed upon Rps27l disruption.
source: Increased Mdm4 ubiquitylation upon Rps27l disruption. Rps27l+/+ or Rps27l−/− MEFs were treated with MG132 before being harvested for IP with Mdm4 Ab or normal IgG control, followed by IB with Mdm4 Ab (top), or for direct IB with indicated Abs (bottom)
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: MDM2-mediated MDM4 ubiquitylation is inhibited by ectopic RPS27L.
source: MDM2-mediated MDM4 ubiquitylation is inhibited by ectopic RPS27L. H1299 cells were transfected with indicated plasmids. At 24 hr post-transfection, cells were treated with MG132 for 4 hr, and then harvested for purification of His-tagged ubiquitylated proteins by Ni-NTA beads, followed by IB with Myc-tag Ab to detect MDM4 ubiquitylation
evidence: This is supported by in vivo ubiquitylation assay data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Shortened Mdm4 protein half-life is observed upon Rps27l disruption.
source: Shortened Mdm4 protein half-life upon Rps27l disruption. Rps27l+/+ or Rps27l−/− MEFs were harvested at various time points post CHX treatment for IB (top). Densitometry quantification was performed with ImageJ, and the decay curves are shown (bottom)
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Increased protein levels of p53 and Mdm2 and decreased protein level of Mdm4 are observed in Rps27l-/- brains.
source: Increased protein levels of p53 and Mdm2 and decreased protein level of Mdm4 in Rps27l−/− brains (D) and livers (E). Brain and liver tissues from P6 pups with indicated genotypes were harvested and lysed for IB
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Increased protein levels of p53 and Mdm2 and decreased protein level of Mdm4 are observed in Rps27l-/- livers.
source: Increased protein levels of p53 and Mdm2 and decreased protein level of Mdm4 in Rps27l−/− brains (D) and livers (E). Brain and liver tissues from P6 pups with indicated genotypes were harvested and lysed for IB
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Deletion of Trp53 rescues postnatal death caused by Rps27l disruption.
source: Deletion of Trp53 rescues postnatal death by Rps27l disruption
evidence: This is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival curve data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Deletion of Trp53 rescues growth retardation caused by Rps27l disruption.
source: Deletion of Trp53 rescues growth retardation and organ hypocellularity. Representative mice at P18 of three genotypes were photographed (B). The bodies (C) were weighed
evidence: This is supported by photographs and body weight measurements shown in Figures 7B and 7C.

claim: Deletion of Trp53 rescues organ hypocellularity caused by Rps27l disruption.
source: Deletion of Trp53 rescues growth retardation and organ hypocellularity...and the total cell numbers (D) of bone marrow (femur and tibia from two hind limbs), spleen, and thymus were counted from P18 mice with genotypes
evidence: This is supported by cell count data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Deletion of Trp53 rescues HSPCs depletion in Rps27l-/- bone marrow.
source: Deletion of Trp53 rescues HSPCs depletion in Rps27l−/− bone marrow. The percentage of LSK, MPP, ST-HSC, and LT-HSC (F); and the percentage of MP, CMP, GMP, and MEP (G) in bone marrow from P18 mice with genotypes
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figures 7F and 7G.

claim: Deletion of Trp53 rescues defects in Rps27l-/- peripheral blood.
source: Deletion of Trp53 rescues defects in Rps27l−/− peripheral blood. CBC classification of peripheral blood from Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/+ (n = 3), Rps27l+/+;Trp53−/− (n = 7), Rps27l+/+;Trp53−/− (n = 10), Rps27l+/−;Trp53−/− (n = 5) mice at P18 was performed
evidence: This is supported by complete blood count data shown in Figure 7H.

claim: Deletion of Trp53 rescues HSPCs depletion in Rps27l-/- fetal livers.
source: Deletion of Trp53 rescues HSPCs depletion in Rps27l−/− fetal livers. Flow cytometry analysis was performed to measure the percentage of HSPCs including LSK (I), MP, CMP, GMP, and MEP (J) in E14.5 fetal livers with genotypes
evidence: This is supported by FACS data shown in Figures 7I and 7J.

claim: Deletion of Trp53 rescues the inability of Rps27l-/- fetal liver cells to reconstitute sterilized bone marrow.
source: Kaplan–Meier survival curves of recipient mice after transplantation. Fetal liver cells (2 × 106 cells) from E14.5 embryos with indicated genotypes were respectively injected into lethally irradiated recipient mice (n = 7 for each genotype). p < 0.0001
evidence: This is supported by transplantation assay data shown in Figure 7K.

claim: Rps27l-/-;Trp53-/- mice have similar survival to Rps27l+/+;Trp53-/- mice.
source: Kaplan–Meier survival curves of Trp53−/− (A) and Trp53+/− (B) mice with three Rps27l genotypes and indicated numbers of mice. p = 0.713 (A)
evidence: This is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival curve data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice have significantly shorter survival than Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/- mice.
source: Kaplan–Meier survival curves of Trp53−/− (A) and Trp53+/− (B) mice with three Rps27l genotypes and indicated numbers of mice. p = 0.713 (A); p = 0.0036 (B)
evidence: This is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival curve data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Lymphomas developed from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice are predominantly T-cell lymphomas.
source: Representative FACS profiles of T cells from lymphomas. Lymphoma cells were isolated and subjected to FACS analysis using Abs against indicated surface markers
evidence: This is supported by FACS data and immunohistochemistry shown in Figure 8D and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Lymphomas from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice exhibit approximately 63% aneuploidy rate.
source: Frequency of diploid and aneuploidy from four tumors developed from Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/− mice with 100 metaphases counted (bottom)
evidence: This is supported by metaphase chromosome counting data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Primary MEFs derived from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- embryos show increased aneuploidy compared to Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/- MEFs.
source: Frequency of diploid and aneuploidy from four pairs of primary MEFs at P2 and P3 derived from Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/− vs Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/− embryos with at least 100 metaphases counted in each sample. Shown are mean ± SD. *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, and ***p < 0.001
evidence: This is supported by metaphase chromosome counting data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: Primary MEFs derived from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- embryos show reduced Trp53 dosage compared to Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/- MEFs.
source: Trp53 dosage in four pairs of primary MEFs at P3 derived from Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/− (R−/−;T+/−) vs Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/− (R+/+;T+/−) embryos. Amounts of p53 DNA in individual MEFs were quantified by qPCR using three sets of primers for exons 5, 6, and 7
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data for Trp53 genomic DNA shown in Figure 8G.

claim: Primary MEFs derived from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/+ embryos do not show increased aneuploidy compared to Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/+ MEFs.
source: Frequency of diploid and aneuploidy from primary MEFs at P2 and P3 derived from Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/+ (n = 7) vs Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/+ (n = 3) individual embryos with at least 100 metaphases counted in each sample. Shown are mean ± SD. p = 0.15
evidence: This is supported by metaphase chromosome counting data shown in Figure 8H.

claim: Increased levels of p53 and p53 targets and decreased levels of Arf are observed upon Rps27l disruption in Trp53+/- MEFs.
source: Increased levels of p53 and p53 targets and decreased levels of Arf upon Rps27l disruption in Trp53+/− MEFs. Primary MEFs at P2 and P3 derived from Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/− and Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/− embryos were left untreated (I) or treated with 5 nM ActD for indicated time periods (J) before being harvested for IB with indicated Abs
evidence: This is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figures 8I and 8J.

claim: In 97% of tumor tissues from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice, the wild-type Trp53 allele was deleted.
source: In 97% of tumor tissues genotyped, wt Trp53 allele was deleted, indicating that Rps27l depletion imposes a selection pressure against p53
evidence: This is supported by PCR amplification data of Trp53 exons shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Rps27l is required for postnatal development of thymus, spleen and bone marrow.
source: Thus, Rps27l is required for postnatal development of some organs, particularly thymus, spleen and bone marrow
evidence: This is inferred from the observed organ hypocellularity and postnatal death in Rps27l-/- mice.

claim: Rps27l disruption causes a moderate increase of p53 that is sufficient to deplete HSPCs in fetal livers and bone marrows.
source: we demonstrated, using a gene-trap mouse model that Rps27l, a p53 downstream ribosomal protein and an Mdm2 E3 ligase substrate, is essential for mouse development. Rps27l disruption causes a moderate increase of p53 which is sufficient to deplete HSPCs in fetal livers and bone marrows, eventually to cause the postnatal death
evidence: This is supported by data showing increased p53 levels and HSPC depletion in Rps27l-/- mice.

claim: A moderate p53 increase is responsible for and sufficient to cause the depletion of HSPCs via inducing apoptosis.
source: Rescuing of these defects by simultaneous deletion of a single or both alleles of Trp53 indicates that p53 plays a causal role and that a moderate p53 increase is responsible for and sufficient to cause the depletion of these HSPCs via inducing apoptosis
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments showing that Trp53 deletion rescues HSPC depletion and apoptosis.

claim: Heterozygous Trp53 deletion is sufficient to rescue postnatal growth retardation and death caused by Rps27l disruption.
source: It is noting worthy that although, unlike homozygous Trp53 deletion, heterozygous Trp53 deletion fails to completely rescue the defects in number or percentage of HSPCs in the bone marrows in p18 weaning mice, it is still sufficient to rescue the postnatal growth retardation and death
evidence: This is supported by survival and growth data showing rescue in Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice.

claim: Rps27l depletion triggers ribosomal stress as evidenced by B23 nucleoplasm staining and enhanced ribosomal protein-Mdm2 binding.
source: Here we reported that Rps27l is indeed a ribosomal protein, whose depletion triggers ribosomal stress (as evidenced by B23 nucleoplasm staining and enhanced RPs-Mdm2 binding) with moderate reduction in ribosomal RNA processing, but no effect on general protein synthesis
evidence: This is supported by B23 immunofluorescence data and co-immunoprecipitation data showing enhanced RP-Mdm2 binding.

claim: Rps27l depletion causes moderate reduction in ribosomal RNA processing.
source: whose depletion triggers ribosomal stress (as evidenced by B23 nucleoplasm staining and enhanced RPs-Mdm2 binding) with moderate reduction in ribosomal RNA processing, but no effect on general protein synthesis
evidence: This is supported by pulse-chase rRNA processing data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Rps27l depletion has no effect on general protein synthesis.
source: with moderate reduction in ribosomal RNA processing, but no effect on general protein synthesis
evidence: This is supported by [35S]-methionine incorporation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: Rps27l actually activates p53 upon disruption, unlike other MDM2-binding ribosomal proteins that activate p53 upon overexpression.
source: We further found, using Rps27l KO model, that unlike in vitro cell culture studies which showed that almost all known MDM2-binding ribosomal proteins acts as p53 activators upon overexpression (Zhang and Lu, 2009; Zhou et al., 2012), Rps27l actually activates p53 upon disruption
evidence: This is supported by data showing p53 accumulation upon Rps27l deletion and rescue of phenotypes by Trp53 deletion.

claim: Rps27l disruption induces p53 in a manner independent of DNA damage.
source: Nevertheless, through this knockout study we conclusively showed that Rps27l disruption induces p53 under the physiological conditions in a manner independent of DNA damage
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that p53 induction occurs without exogenous DNA damage and is mediated through ribosomal stress.

claim: p53 induction triggered by Rps27l disruption is dependent on Rpl11 but independent of Rpl5.
source: It is also interesting in our finding that consistent with enhanced binding of Mdm2-Rpl11, but not Mdm2-Rpl5, p53 induction triggered by Rps27l disruption is dependent of Rpl11, but independent of Rpl5
evidence: This is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments showing that Rpl11 silencing abrogates p53 activation while Rpl5 silencing does not.

claim: Rps27l has no direct effect on Mdm2 mRNA transcription.
source: For first question, we found that while Rps27l has no direct effect on Mdm2 mRNA transcription, it indeed negatively regulates the Mdm2 protein stability
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data showing no change in Mdm2 mRNA levels.

claim: Rps27l negatively regulates Mdm2 protein stability with Mdm2 protein half-life being extended or shortened upon Rps27l depletion or overexpression, respectively.
source: it indeed negatively regulates the Mdm2 protein stability with Mdm2 protein half-life being extended or shortened upon Rps27l depletion or overexpression, respectively
evidence: This is supported by cycloheximide chase assays in MEFs and H1299 cells.

claim: In wild-type cells under unstressed conditions, Rps27l binds to Mdm2 on its acidic domain.
source: It is conceivable that in wt cells under unstressed conditions, Rps27l binds to Mdm2 on its acidic domain (Xiong et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work (Xiong et al., 2011).

claim: Upon Rps27l disruption, other ribosomal proteins are released from nucleoli and bind to Mdm2 to inhibit Mdm2 self-ubiquitylation, leading to its stabilization.
source: Upon Rps27l disruption, which triggers ribosomal stress, other ribosomal proteins are released from nucleoli and bind to Mdm2 on an unoccupied acidic domain to inhibit Mdm2 self-ubiquitylation, leading to its stabilization
evidence: This is an inference based on data showing enhanced RP-Mdm2 binding, reduced Mdm2 self-ubiquitylation, and extended Mdm2 half-life.

claim: Mdm2-mediated Mdm4 ubiquitylation and degradation is negatively regulated by Rps27l.
source: We also showed by both loss-of-function and rescue-of-function studies that Mdm2-mediated Mdm4 ubiquitylation and degradation is negatively regulated by Rps27l, being enhanced upon Rps27l depletion and reduced upon RPS27L overexpression
evidence: This is supported by ubiquitylation assays and protein half-life measurements.

claim: Enhanced Mdm2-ribosomal protein binding as a result of ribosomal stress in response to Rps27l disruption facilitates Mdm2-dependent Mdm4 degradation.
source: Thus, enhanced Mdm2-RPs binding (such as Mdm2-Rpl11 binding) as a result of ribosomal stress in response to Rps27l disruption would facilitate Mdm2-dependent Mdm4 degradation, which is consistent with a previous observation (Gilkes et al., 2006)
evidence: This is an inference based on data showing enhanced Mdm2-RP binding and increased Mdm4 degradation, supported by citation to Gilkes et al., 2006.

claim: Although Mdm2-Mdm4 has better affinity upon Rps27l deletion, a much reduced amount of Mdm4 results in reduced level of Mdm2-bound Mdm4.
source: Furthermore, we found that although Mdm2-Mdm4 has a better affinity upon Rps27l deletion, a much reduced amount of Mdm4 in Rps27l−/− MEFs results in a reduced level of Mdm2-bound Mdm4, thus lesser formation of the Mdm2-Mdm4 heterodimer
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data showing reduced Mdm2-Mdm4 complex despite higher binding affinity.

claim: Compromised Mdm2-Mdm4 ligase activity in Rps27l-/- MEFs leads to reduced p53 ubiquitylation and degradation, consequently an extended p53 protein half-life and increased p53 levels.
source: Given that Mdm2-Mdm4 heterodimer is the most stable and active form of E3 ligase for targeted p53 degradation, as shown in both in vitro (Kawai et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2011) and in vivo (Francoz et al., 2006; Garcia et al., 2011; Huang et al., 2011; Pant et al., 2011) studies, compromised Mdm2-Mdm4 ligase activity in Rps27l−/− MEFs leads to a reduced p53 ubiquitylation and degradation, consequently an extended p53 protein half-life and increased p53 levels
evidence: This is an inference based on data showing reduced Mdm2-Mdm4 complex, reduced p53 ubiquitylation, extended p53 half-life, and increased p53 levels, supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Rps27l disruption causes a moderate increase of p53 that is insufficient to induce embryonic lethality but sufficient to induce postnatal lethality.
source: In contrast, Rps27l disruption causes a moderate increase of p53 which is insufficient to induce embryonic lethality, but sufficient to induce postnatal lethality, resulting from apoptotic depletion of HPSCs in both fetal liver and neonatal bone marrow
evidence: This is supported by survival data and HSPC analysis showing postnatal death but not embryonic lethality.

claim: Postnatal death upon Rps27l disruption occurs under the wild-type background of Rps27 and other ribosomal genes encoding Mdm2-binding ribosomal proteins.
source: It is worth noting that postnatal death upon Rps27l disruption occurs under the wt background of its family member, Rps27 as well as other ribosomal genes encoding all known Mdm2-binding ribosomal proteins
evidence: This is an inference based on the fact that only Rps27l was disrupted in the knockout model.

claim: For hematopoiesis, Rps27l plays a non-redundant role in reducing p53 levels via stabilizing the Mdm2-Mdm4 complex.
source: Thus, for hematopoiesis, Rps27l plays a non-redundant role in reducing p53 levels via stabilizing the Mdm2-Mdm4 complex
evidence: This is an inference based on the inability of other ribosomal proteins to compensate for Rps27l loss.

claim: Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice have a much higher incidence than Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/- mice to develop spontaneous T-lymphoblastic and B-cell lymphomas.
source: Surprisingly, while moderate p53 increase is expected to decrease the tumor incidence as shown in Mdm2 hypomorphic mice (Mendrysa et al., 2006) and in Mdm2+/− or Mdm4+/− mice (Alt et al., 2003; Terzian et al., 2007), our Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/− mice have a much higher incidence than Rps27l+/+;Trp53+/− mice to develop spontaneous T-lymphoblastic and in rare case B-cell lymphomas, resulting in a shortened life-span
evidence: This is supported by Kaplan-Meier survival data and tumor analysis.

claim: The genome of lymphoma cells from Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice is highly unstable with an aneuploidy rate of approximately 63%.
source: Furthermore, the genome of these lymphoma cells is highly unstable with a strike aneuploidy rate of ∼63%, which is remarkably higher than those derived from Trp53-null mice with an aneuploidy rate of 30–35% (Kibe et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by metaphase chromosome counting data and comparison to published data.

claim: Rps27l is required for the maintenance of genomic stability.
source: Thus, our study provides an in vivo demonstration that Rps27l is required for the maintenance of genomic stability, which is consistent with a previous report, showing that RPS27L knockdown in HCT116 colon cancer cells may trigger genomic instability (Li et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by aneuploidy data in lymphomas and MEFs, and citation to Li et al., 2007.

claim: Genomic instability occurs in early passage primary MEFs with the genotype of Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/-, but not of Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/+.
source: One more striking observation we made in this study is that the genomic instability occurs in early passage primary MEFs with the genotype of Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/−, but not of Rps27l−/−;Trp53+/+
evidence: This is supported by metaphase chromosome counting data in MEFs shown in Figures 8F and 8H.

claim: Rps27l plays a limited role in the maintenance of genomic stability if p53 is normal.
source: In other word, Rps27l plays a limited role in the maintenance of genomic stability, if p53 is normal
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that genomic instability is not observed in Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/+ MEFs.

claim: When one allele of Trp53 is deleted or mutated, Rps27l becomes critically essential in preventing the loss of p53 heterozygosity.
source: However, when one allele of Trp53 is deleted or mutated (such as in the case of Li-Fraumeni syndrome or at various stage of tumorigenesis), Rps27l becomes critically essential in preventing the loss of p53 heterozygosity
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Rps27l loss leads to genomic instability and p53 LOH specifically in the Trp53+/- background.

claim: Loss or decreased expression of Rps27l would exacerbate genomic instability and provide selection pressure against p53, eventually leading to tumor development.
source: Thus, its loss or decreased expression by any means would exacerbate genomic instability and provide selection pressure against p53, eventually leading to tumor development
evidence: This is inferred from the observed genomic instability, p53 LOH, and increased tumor incidence in Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice.

claim: High level of RPS27L expression predicted a better prognosis in colon cancer patients.
source: Potential tumor suppressive function of RPS27L is further supported by an observation that high level of RPS27L expression predicted a better prognosis in colon cancer patients (Huang et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Huang et al., 2013.

claim: In normal cells with wild-type p53, Rps27l stabilizes the Mdm2-Mdm4 heterodimer to form an optimal E3 ligase complex for effective p53 ubiquitylation and degradation.
source: In normal cell with wild-type p53 (Trp53+/+), Rps27l, upon induction by p53 in response to various stresses, stabilizes the Mdm2-Mdm4 heterodimer to form an optimal E3 ligase complex for effective p53 ubiquitylation and degradation, thus keeping p53 level in check, leading to normal growth and development
evidence: This is a summary model based on all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Rps27l disruption causes an imbalance in ribosomal protein levels and triggers ribosomal stress to stabilize Mdm2.
source: Rps27l+/+ disruption causes an imbalance in ribosomal protein levels and triggers ribosomal stress to stabilize Mdm2
evidence: This is a summary model based on data showing B23 release, enhanced RP-Mdm2 binding, and Mdm2 stabilization.

claim: Increased Mdm2 adapts a conformation that favors Mdm4 ubiquitylation, leading to a reduced Mdm2-Mdm4 complex and compromised p53 ubiquitylation.
source: Increased Mdm2 adapts a conformation that favors the Mdm4 ubiquitylation, leading to a reduced Mdm2-Mdm4 complex and compromised p53 ubiquitylation with an ultimate increase in p53
evidence: This is a summary model based on data showing increased Mdm4 ubiquitylation, reduced Mdm2-Mdm4 complex, and reduced p53 ubiquitylation.

claim: Moderately increased p53 is sufficient to induce growth retardation and apoptosis by transactivating p21 and Puma, respectively.
source: Moderately increased p53 is sufficient to induce growth retardation and apoptosis by transactivating p21 and Puma, respectively, leading to the depletion of HSPCs and bone marrow, and eventually postnatal death
evidence: This is a summary model based on data showing increased p21 and Puma expression, apoptosis, HSPC depletion, and postnatal death.

claim: In cancer-prone cells with Trp53+/- status, Rps27l plays an essential role in keeping genome integrity.
source: In cancer-prone cells with a Trp53+/− status, Rps27l plays an essential role in keeping genome integrity
evidence: This is a summary model based on data showing genomic instability in Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- cells.

claim: Rps27l disruption triggers genomic instability, followed by selection for Trp53 deletion, leading to spontaneous lymphoma.
source: Rps27l+/− disruption triggers genomic instability, followed by selection for Trp53 deletion. The cells with Trp53 deleted are selected for and outgrow to form spontaneous lymphoma
evidence: This is a summary model based on data showing genomic instability, p53 LOH, and lymphoma development in Rps27l-/-;Trp53+/- mice.
